title: Reverse Bits
description: Given a 32-bit unsigned integer `n`, reverse the order of its 32 bits and return the result as an unsigned integer. Always treat the value as exactly 32 bits, including leading zeros.
hints: Build the answer one bit at a time, from the lowest bit of n to the highest.
The lowest bit of n should become the highest bit of the answer, so shift the result left as you go.
Repeat exactly 32 times: res = (res << 1) | (n & 1), then n >>= 1.

solution.explanation: Loop exactly 32 times. In each step shift the result left by one, append the lowest bit of n using OR with n & 1, then shift n right. After 32 steps the first bit read (the least significant) sits in the most significant position. Because the number of iterations is fixed, time and space are O(1). Looping a fixed 32 times is what keeps leading zeros correct.
